sources.entry: pipx - Install and run Python applications in isolated environments. Like npx in Node.js.

summary.one_liner: pipx installs and runs Python command-line applications, each in its own isolated environment, so their dependencies don't conflict.
summary.what_it_does: pipx installs Python packages that provide command-line applications and exposes their entrypoints while keeping each app in an isolated environment. The install command sets up an app and its dependencies separately, and uninstalling removes them cleanly. It can list, upgrade, and uninstall apps it installed. The run command executes the latest version of an application in a temporary environment without installing it permanently. According to the README, pipx runs with regular user permissions and does not need sudo pip install. The README notes it installs with uv when available and pip otherwise.
use_cases: install Python command-line tools without dependency conflicts
run a Python CLI app once without installing it
upgrade or uninstall globally available Python tools
try out a Python application in a temporary environment
notable: Runs Python apps in isolated per-app environments with clean uninstalls
run command executes an application in a temporary environment without installing it
Runs with regular user permissions, no sudo pip install
Installs with uv when available, falls back to pip
caveats: Focused on applications that run from the command line; not a general library dependency manager
README gives install commands for macOS (brew), Windows (scoop), and Linux via distribution package managers
